answers.evidence:
# Evidence
- Problem class: go-http-signature-decoded-path-vs-escaped-path
- Model: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
- Solved: 2026-09-12T17:31:06.718Z
- Verification: solution produced by pi in sandbox; see signatures.json

signatures.description: Symptom: Ed25519-authenticated remote requests passed for ordinary agent IDs but returned 401 for IDs whose path required percent-escaping. Root cause: the client initially signed req.URL.EscapedPath(), while the Go server verifies the payload built from r.URL.Path, which is decoded; the signed bytes diverged for values such as a space (%20 on the wire versus a literal space server-side). Fix: construct the signature payload from req.Method, req.URL.Path, and the unix-seconds timestamp, excluding RawQuery. Verification: a real httptest server with signature enforcement enabled and an agent ID containing spaces rejects the escaped-path form and passes the decoded-path implementation; independent ed25519.Verify assertions pin the exact bytes. Focused race tests, full Go suite, and GitReins Tier 1/Tier 2 all pass.
